topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Biology and Lecture Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the multi-lecture course by introducing the general objectives, clinical context, and specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Normal Tissue Differentiation and Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core biological definition of cancer as a breakdown of multicellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Benign-to-Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors breach tissue boundaries, disseminate to distant organs, and progress along the spectrum from benign precursor lesions to invasive malignancies.

topics.label: Nomenclature of Benign and Malignant Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions used to classify and name tumors based on tissue origin and malignancy.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Morbidity and Mortality in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological and anatomical mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause systemic disease and patient death.

topics.label: Patterns of Tumor Incidence Across Tissues and Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the epidemiological frequency of various tumor types in humans with tumor incidence across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Clinical Modalities of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the rationale, benefits, and practical limitations of population screening programs for identifying precursor lesions and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Conclusion and Practical Session Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping details for subsequent practicals and lectures.
